the development of strategies that will assist individuals to make healthier food choices, and to reduce their exposure to fast-food outlets.
the identification of the beliefs and perceptions that underpin fast food choice.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

fast-food consumption is not necessarily a result of a lack of knowledge, or a lack of motivation, but rather, that the decision-making process is more complicated and multifaceted than previously thought.
the Theory of Planned Behavior is a useful tool in understanding and explaining food choice behavior.
the findings of the present study are consistent with the Theory of Planned behaviour and the results of other studies that examined fast food choice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the findings suggest the need to address the affective and social dimensions of fast-food consumption.
the Theory of Planned Behavior does not fully explain the beliefs and perceptions that influence fast food consumption in Australia.
the consumption of fast food is a complex phenomenon that is not solely determined by the perceived health consequences of eating fast food.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health benefits of eating fast food are outweighed by the health risks.
the decision to eat fast food is complex, and is driven by multiple factors that are not always rational or health-oriented.
fast food is not just about the food.
